The guitar battente (chitarra battente) is an Italian chordophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 321.322, of the guitar family; its form resembles the five-course Baroque guitar but larger. Brass strings were traditional and steel is now usual; there are commonly five or four courses of two or three strings, and the tuning may put the lower strings higher. It is played without a pick, by plucking and strumming with the fingers and striking the strings or the soundboard. It is now mostly played by folk musicians in southern Italy, in Calabria, Apulia, Basilicata and Campania, to accompany singing or dancing, and it can also be played solo or in an ensemble.
